notes:
Status: Closed-lost (decision communicated 2026-02-26) — selected competitor LatticeFlux. Short summary: Silverpine ran a 3-week POC (doc-search + structured response layer + tool-calling for knowledge lookups). Initial impressions were positive (fast latency, good embedding recall), but during final eval the incumbent model they had in prod (internal LatticeFlux-backed pipeline) showed higher fidelity for structured outputs and predictable tool-calls. After Redwood's model upgrade (2026-02-10) they saw a quality regression: schema field ordering changed, occasional missing fields, and non-deterministic tool-call sequences that broke downstream parsers.

Key quotes / signal: "We can't trust unpredictable tool outputs — too risky for customer-facing answers" — Tomás Vega (Head of Engineering). Security also escalated because our tool-calling approach required short-lived creds to third-party search services; their InfoSec flagged the pattern and preferred LatticeFlux's integrated connector model (no external ephemeral creds). Budget team then put procurement on hold pending a security re-eval; meanwhile the internal champion (Sr. ML Engineer, Priya Rao) left for another role mid-eval which removed momentum.

What we did: rapid patch to schema enforcement (2026-02-12), added end-to-end deterministic tool-call tests, provided a security design doc and a short demo of vault/KMS flow (drive link). Ran remediation POC with constrained model variant and additional post-processing SRO (structured response orchestration) — results improved but not in time for their procurement calendar.

Why we lost: primary reason = perceived quality regression vs their incumbent in structured outputs + security concerns around our tool-calling pattern. Secondary = no internal champion after departure and a budget freeze for H1. Competitive note: LatticeFlux emphasized turnkey connectors + strict schema guarantees in their demo which resonated with their product managers.

Timeline (selected):
- 2025-10-01: Initial inbound; scoping call (AE: Maya).
- 2025-11-15: Tech deep-dive w/ SE Arjun.
- 2026-01-08: POC kickoff (3-week, hosted API)
- 2026-02-10: Redwood model upgrade during POC — regression observed.
- 2026-02-12: Hotfix + schema enforcement patch deployed.
- 2026-02-18: Security review escalation; requested vault/KMS design.
- 2026-02-22: Business decision meeting; procurement freezes.
- 2026-02-26: Vendor selection communicated — closed-lost to LatticeFlux.

Follow-ups / win-back opportunities: keep quarterly check-ins; provide a short case study demonstrating deterministic tool-calling and schema guarantees for doc-search customers; propose a limited pilot with on-prem connector and signed security SLA. Capture lessons learned in deal post-mortem (attached links).
